# CadForge vs. AutoCAD: parity benchmark

*Generated by `python3 tools/benchmark/score.py --write`; do not edit by hand. Rubric: `tools/benchmark/rubric.tsv`.*

**Composite score: 71.1 / 100.**

This number is a self-assessment against a written rubric, not a measurement against AutoCAD itself (AutoCAD cannot be run or downloaded in the build environment). It is meant to be reproducible and hard to inflate: the command axes are computed from the program's own command registry, the test axis from the test sources, and every credit in the checklists points at code or a test that `score.py --check` verifies still exists.

## Scores

| Axis | What is measured | Weight | Score | Points |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Command breadth: core inventory | registry vs. acad-commands.tsv (usage-weighted) | 10 | 99.2% | 9.9 |
| Command breadth: long tail | registry vs. acad-longtail.tsv (usage-weighted) | 10 | 25.7% | 2.6 |
| Command aliases (acad.pgp) | registry vs. acad-aliases.tsv | 2 | 100.0% | 2.0 |
| Commands exercised by automated tests | registered commands named by a test | 8 | 93.3% | 7.5 |
| Object types and drawing model | checklist | 8 | 68.2% | 5.5 |
| File formats and interchange | checklist | 10 | 73.7% | 7.4 |
| Drafting aids, selection, inquiry | checklist | 8 | 78.9% | 6.3 |
| User interface and workflow | checklist | 12 | 77.5% | 9.3 |
| Annotation, styles and symbols | checklist | 7 | 53.5% | 3.7 |
| Layouts, plotting and output | checklist | 6 | 63.9% | 3.8 |
| 3D modelling | checklist | 5 | 64.3% | 3.2 |
| Reliability and performance | checklist | 6 | 82.5% | 4.9 |
| Extensibility and automation | checklist | 5 | 56.7% | 2.8 |
| Platform and distribution | checklist | 3 | 70.8% | 2.1 |
| **Composite** | | **100** | | **71.1** |

Command inventory: 286 core commands (weighted by how often drawings use them) and 182 long-tail commands. 282 / 286 core and 41 / 182 long-tail commands exist in the registry; commands that only report "not supported" earn part of their weight (`tools/benchmark/stubs.tsv`). All 100% of the standard `acad.pgp` aliases resolve to the right command.

Test inventory: 638 Rust tests and 36 browser tests (headless Chromium driving the WebAssembly build).

## How to read it

- **Breadth** axes count commands that exist. They say nothing about how deep a command goes; the *tested* axis only credits a command when a test types it.
- **Checklists** list AutoCAD capabilities. Full credit means the capability is present and tested; partial credit names what is missing in the last column.
- The long-tail inventory is deliberately uncomfortable: it contains specialist features (meshes, surfaces, sheet sets, rendering, VBA...) that a 2D-first drafting program does not offer. They weigh 10 of the 100 points.
- The score counts only what is built. It does not reward things AutoCAD lacks, and it cannot measure feel, polish or the thousands of small behaviours of a 40-year-old product.

## What stands between this and 95

Points still on the table, largest first (checklist items below full credit):

- 0.67 pt: Per-viewport layer overrides (output) - reported as unsupported by LAYER / VPLAYER
- 0.67 pt: Pen assignments and plot style tables (output) - not implemented
- 0.60 pt: User interface customization (ui) - not implemented
- 0.60 pt: Interface in other languages (ui) - English only
- 0.60 pt: Touch and pen input (ui) - not implemented
- 0.60 pt: Indexed selection and rendering for very large drawings (reliability) - linear scans over the entity list
- 0.56 pt: .NET / ObjectARX plugin API (extend) - not implemented
- 0.56 pt: COM / ActiveX / VBA automation (extend) - not implemented
- 0.53 pt: Binary DXF (io) - not implemented
- 0.53 pt: DWG read and write (io) - not implemented: the format is proprietary
- 0.53 pt: Plot style tables (CTB / STB) and device drivers (io) - not implemented
- 0.53 pt: SAT, STEP, IGES, FBX, 3DS and other exchange formats (io) - not implemented
- 0.50 pt: Cloud storage and collaboration (platform) - not implemented
- 0.42 pt: Geometric and dimensional constraints (drafting) - not implemented
- 0.42 pt: UI customization and workspaces (extend) - workspaces only
- 0.41 pt: Annotative objects and scale lists (annotation) - not implemented
- 0.41 pt: Dynamic blocks: parameters, actions, visibility states (annotation) - not implemented
- 0.41 pt: Table formulas and data links (annotation) - not implemented
- 0.41 pt: Sheet set manager (annotation) - not implemented
- 0.41 pt: CAD standards checking (annotation) - not implemented
- 0.36 pt: Dimensions that follow the geometry they measure (objects) - dimensions keep their own definition points
- 0.36 pt: PDF, DGN and DWF underlays (objects) - not implemented
- 0.36 pt: OLE objects (objects) - not implemented
- 0.36 pt: 3D polylines, 3D lines and Z coordinates on every object (objects) - entities are 2D; only solids have a third dimension
- 0.36 pt: Meshes, surfaces and point clouds (objects) - not implemented

Long-tail commands that do not exist yet are listed by `cargo run -p cadforge-engine --example parity -- --missing`. Many are tied to features this program does not have at all (meshes and surfaces, sheet sets, annotative scaling, dynamic blocks, PDF / DGN underlays, DWG, VBA / .NET, rendering). Closing the gap to 95 means building those, not polishing what is here; some of them (DWG, the plug-in ecosystem, 40 years of drawings and habits) cannot be reproduced at all.

## Out of scope (by decision)

These rubric items were taken out of the score by the project owner. They no longer count in their axis; the other items in that axis now carry the weight.

- Mobile apps (platform): Not needed: the project owner said no mobile app is wanted (2026-10-22)
